todays_goal: Begin the 2026-27 school year with clear understanding in each scheduled subject.

lessons.subject: mathematics
lessons.previous_learning: Place value with decimals and whole-number multiplication.
learning_objectives: Multiply decimals by whole numbers and other decimals.
Divide decimals by whole numbers with understanding of place value.
Estimate products and quotients to check reasonableness.
lessons.why_it_matters: Decimal operations appear in money, measurement, and science data throughout Grade 6.

vocabulary.definition: A reasonable approximation before exact calculation.

lessons.written_instruction: Work through decimal multiplication and division using place-value reasoning.

worked_examples.title: Divide 5.04 / 4
worked_examples.explanation: Divide as whole numbers, then place the decimal using place value.

exit_ticket.prompt: Explain why estimating 5.04 / 4 helps before dividing.
exit_ticket.answer: Estimation checks whether the quotient near 1.25 is reasonable.

lessons.voice_prompt: Connect to whole-number operations, teach decimal placement, model two full examples, then guide practice verbally.

lessons.subject: literature
lessons.lesson_title: Informational text / central idea and evidence
lessons.previous_learning: Prior Grade 6 work in this course.
learning_objectives: Identify the central idea of an informational passage.
lessons.why_it_matters: This skill supports Grade 6 reasoning and future units.

worked_examples.title: Central idea in a short article
worked_examples.problem: Read about how bees pollinate crops.
worked_examples.solution: Central idea: Bees help plants reproduce by moving pollen.
worked_examples.explanation: Evidence includes descriptions of pollen transfer and crop dependence.

guided_practice.prompt: State the central idea in one sentence.
guided_practice.hint: What is the passage mostly about?

independent_practice.prompt: List two pieces of evidence for the central idea.

exit_ticket.prompt: What is the difference between a topic and a central idea?
exit_ticket.answer: A topic is the subject; the central idea is the main point the author makes about it.

lessons.voice_prompt: Model finding central idea and evidence in a short passage.

lessons.subject: writing
lessons.previous_learning: Prior Grade 6 work in this course.
learning_objectives: Write a paragraph with a clear topic sentence and evidence.
Explain how evidence supports the claim.
lessons.why_it_matters: This skill supports Grade 6 reasoning and future units.

worked_examples.title: Explanatory paragraph model
worked_examples.problem: Explain why reading daily improves vocabulary.
worked_examples.solution: Topic sentence + two evidence sentences + explanation.
worked_examples.explanation: Each evidence sentence connects back to the claim.

guided_practice.prompt: Draft a topic sentence for an explanatory paragraph.

independent_practice.prompt: Write a full explanatory paragraph with two pieces of evidence.

exit_ticket.prompt: What must every evidence sentence do?
exit_ticket.answer: Support and connect to the topic sentence/claim.

lessons.subject: science
lessons.lesson_title: How light lets us see objects
lessons.previous_learning: Prior Grade 6 work in this course.
learning_objectives: Explain that we see objects when light reflects into our eyes.
Describe the role of light sources and reflected light.
lessons.why_it_matters: This skill supports Grade 6 reasoning and future units.

worked_examples.title: Seeing a book
worked_examples.problem: Why can you see a book on a desk?
worked_examples.solution: Light reflects from the book into your eyes.
worked_examples.explanation: The book is not a light source; it reflects light from another source.

guided_practice.prompt: Name one light source and one object seen by reflected light.

independent_practice.prompt: Explain why the moon is visible at night.

exit_ticket.prompt: What must happen for you to see an object?
exit_ticket.answer: Light must enter your eyes, usually by reflection from the object.

lessons.voice_prompt: Use concrete examples; distinguish sources from reflectors.

lessons.subject: history_geography
lessons.previous_learning: Prior Grade 6 work in this course.
learning_objectives: Describe how mountains and seas shaped Greek city-states.
Locate major geographic features on a map.
lessons.why_it_matters: This skill supports Grade 6 reasoning and future units.

worked_examples.title: Mountains and city-states
worked_examples.problem: How did mountains affect Greek political organization?
worked_examples.solution: Mountains separated communities, encouraging independent city-states.
worked_examples.explanation: Geography influenced trade, travel, and political unity.

guided_practice.prompt: Name two geographic features of Greece and one effect of each.

independent_practice.prompt: Explain how the Aegean Sea helped Greek trade.

exit_ticket.prompt: Why did Greece develop city-states instead of one large empire?
exit_ticket.answer: Mountainous terrain separated regions and made unified rule difficult.

lessons.voice_prompt: Connect geography to daily life in ancient Greece.

lessons.subject: french
lessons.previous_learning: Prior Grade 6 work in this course.
learning_objectives: Conjugate regular -ER verbs in present tense.
Form simple negative sentences with ne...pas.
lessons.why_it_matters: This skill supports Grade 6 reasoning and future units.

worked_examples.title: Je parle / Je ne parle pas
worked_examples.problem: Conjugate parler for je; make negative.
worked_examples.solution: Je parle. Je ne parle pas.
worked_examples.explanation: Remove -er, add -e for je; wrap verb with ne...pas for negation.

guided_practice.prompt: Say: I do not speak French.

exit_ticket.prompt: Where do ne and pas go around the verb?
exit_ticket.answer: ne before the conjugated verb, pas after it.

lessons.voice_prompt: Use French pronunciation, short exchanges, gentle correction.

lessons.subject: computer_science
lessons.previous_learning: Prior Grade 6 work in this course.
learning_objectives: Read and draw flowcharts with decision diamonds.
Explain how conditionals change program flow.
lessons.why_it_matters: This skill supports Grade 6 reasoning and future units.

worked_examples.title: If score >= 60 pass
worked_examples.solution: Start -> input score -> decision -> pass or fail -> end
worked_examples.explanation: The decision diamond branches based on a condition.

guided_practice.prompt: What shape means a decision in a flowchart?

independent_practice.prompt: Draw a flowchart for choosing a jacket if temperature < 50.

exit_ticket.prompt: What does a conditional do in an algorithm?
exit_ticket.answer: It chooses different paths based on whether a condition is true or false.

lessons.subject: pe
lessons.previous_learning: Prior Grade 6 work in this course.
learning_objectives: Demonstrate basic movement patterns with control.
lessons.why_it_matters: This skill supports Grade 6 reasoning and future units.

worked_examples.title: Warm-up sequence
worked_examples.solution: Light jog, dynamic stretches, movement prep.
worked_examples.explanation: Warm-up prepares muscles and focus before activity.

guided_practice.prompt: Name two dynamic stretches and their purpose.

independent_practice.prompt: Complete the warm-up and note one area to improve.

exit_ticket.prompt: Why warm up before athletic activity?
exit_ticket.answer: To reduce injury risk and prepare the body to move effectively.
